study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify brain-structural heterogeneity in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder by mapping individual deviations from a normative model, and assess how group-level analyses may mask inter-individual abnormalities.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that all participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study. This is the dataset name used for both healthy controls and patients.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study from October 27, 2004, to October 17, 2012.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Individual deviations from the normative model were frequent but highly heterogeneous in both schizophrenia and bipolar disorder; overlap >2% occurred only in few loci, with schizophrenia showing mean gray matter reductions in frontal, temporal, and cerebellar regions and bipolar disorder primarily in cerebellum.
